correctness.rationale: The proof establishes n=qa+r belongs to the interval semigroup exactly when r<=qk, with both directions justified. The double/triple conditions give exact lower bounds; their dominance swaps precisely at r=ceil(2a/3), with r<ceil(a/2) excluded. The resulting two-band integer intervals and finite sum include all boundaries. Ceiling bounds yield |F-2a^2/(9k)|<3a and |g-a^2/(2k)|<a for every a>=2, 1<=k<a, hence F/g->4/9 if k=o(a). A separate unbounded-coin dynamic program exactly agreed for all 5886 pairs with 2<=a<110, covering 566195 fundamental gaps, and checked both error bounds. Tests corroborate rather than prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: Fundamental gaps are the divisibility-maximal missing integers that determine the entire numerical semigroup by their divisor closure. This is a natural structural invariant distinct from the genus, the isolated-gap predicate and the pseudo-Frobenius type. The theorem describes every such gap in an infinite two-parameter family and proves an unexpectedly universal 4/9 fraction for all sublinear generator interval widths, giving a nontrivial cross-family asymptotic with uniform error.
